rules.title: Residential rental application screening fee cap and refunds
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may charge a residential rental applicant only for the actual out-of-pocket costs and reasonable time spent screening the applicant, capped at $30 per applicant as CPI-adjusted. The landlord must provide an itemized receipt, return unused amounts if no reference check or credit report is obtained, and provide any consumer credit report to the applicant within seven days of receiving it.
rules.key_value: Actual out-of-pocket costs and reasonable time, capped at $30 per applicant, adjusted annually by CPI beginning January 1, 1998

coverage.summary: Applies when a landlord or agent receives a request to rent residential rental property and charges an application screening fee.

rules.interaction: The section states it does not preempt federal or state housing-assistance program rules on deposits and fees and does not prevent a landlord from accepting a reusable screening report under Section 1950.1.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.

rules.title: Application screening process conditions when charging a screening fee
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent charging an application screening fee must either use a written-criteria, first-qualified-applicant process in the order completed applications are received and charge only when an application is actually considered, or return the entire fee to any applicant not selected. A landlord or agent may not charge a screening fee when they know or should know no rental unit is available or will be available within a reasonable time.
rules.key_value: First qualified applicant in order received, or refund entire fee to unselected applicants within 7 days of selecting a tenant or 30 days of application submission, whichever occurs first

coverage.summary: Applies to landlords or agents charging residential rental application screening fees.

rules.exemptions: A landlord or agent who inadvertently collects a fee because of multiple concurrent application submissions does not violate the rule if the fee is refunded within seven days to an applicant whose application is not considered, or the applicant chooses to apply the fee to another rental unit offered by the landlord.
rules.interaction: The section states it does not preempt federal or state housing-assistance program rules on deposits and fees and does not prevent a landlord from accepting a reusable screening report under Section 1950.1.
